title: quadlet: do not set RemainAfterExit=yes for volume units by default
body:
fixes #27862

### Summary
Quadlet previously set `RemainAfterExit=yes` by default when converting `.volume` unit files into systemd oneshot services. 

Because `RemainAfterExit=yes` keeps the service unit in the `active (exited)` state, if a volume is deleted (e.g. to update volume options) and a dependent container service is restarted, systemd skips re-executing the volume service since it is already marked active.

### Changes
- Updated `ConvertVolume()` in `pkg/systemd/quadlet/quadlet.go` to pass `false` for `remainAfterExit`.
- Updated Quadlet test fixture assertion in `test/e2e/quadlet/basic.volume`.

### Checklist
- [x] Code is signed off (`git commit -s`)
- [x] Tests pass / modified test updated

comments.body: In general, I don't like changing default behaviours as it changes how existing implementations act. Having said that, this change does make sense. @podman-container-tools/core-maintainers WDYT?
I just realized it was my suggestion to begin with. But, still I would like to get additional approvals

I'm LGTM. We can get a few more acks from maintainers for the behavior change before we merge, though.
@podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers PTAL

Thanks @Luap99 for the architectural feedback!

That makes complete sense regarding backward compatibility and systemd dependency behavior across oneshot unit types (`.volume`, `.network`, `.image`, `.build`). Changing default behavior for existing volume units could break existing setups relying on `ActiveState=active`.

Would adding an explicit `RemainAfterExit=` key option (defaulting to `yes` to preserve backward compatibility, but allowing users to set `RemainAfterExit=no` in `.volume` / `.network` files when they need re-creation on restart) be a cleaner, safer opt-in approach?

I've also updated the description to `Fixes #27862`.

I would change the default for Volume units only. `podman volume create --ignore` is cheap and idempotent; there is no `VolumeDeleteOnStop`, and `.build` already did this. Network/image/artifact stay `RemainAfterExit=yes`. And document it.

Thanks @Honny1! I've updated `docs/source/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.md` to document that `.volume` oneshot units do not set `RemainAfterExit=yes` by default (matching `.build` behavior while leaving `.network`, `.image`, and `.artifact` units unchanged). 

Pushed the documentation update to the PR!
